subject: ENT

subject: ENT

stem: A 3-month-old has coryza and fever progressing to tachypnea, wheeze, chest retractions and nasal flaring. Chest is hyperinflated with fine crackles; RSV is detected. What is the mainstay of management?
opts: Supportive: oxygen, nasal suction, hydration; no routine bronchodilators

subject: ENT
topic: Tuning fork - Weber to affected side in conductive loss; Rinne negative
stem: On tuning-fork testing, a patient has Weber lateralizing to the LEFT ear, and Rinne is NEGATIVE on the left (BC > AC) but POSITIVE on the right. Which statement is correct?

stem: A 75-year-old man with advanced Parkinson's disease and dysphagia presents with fever and cough. He is found to have right lower lobe consolidation. Which of the following best describes the likely microbiology of this pneumonia?

subject: ENT

subject: ENT
topic: Acute bacterial rhinosinusitis - 'double worsening' / persistence criteria

opts: Symptoms that worsened after initially improving, or persist beyond 10 days with purulence and facial pain ('double worsening')

subject: ENT
stem: A patient with sweat chloride test positive for developing recurrent chest infection, otitis media and diarrhea and there is bronchial wall thickening. Pseudomonas was isolated. What is the diagnosis?

subject: ENT
topic: Local anesthetic cardiotoxicity — bupivacaine vs lidocaine
stem: A 40-year-old woman receives epidural anesthesia with bupivacaine for labor analgesia. She develops perioral numbness, tinnitus, and then a seizure. ECG shows wide QRS. What property of bupivacaine explains its higher cardiotoxicity compared with lidocaine?
opts: Bupivacaine is metabolized by plasma pseudocholinesterase
Bupivacaine is a weaker sodium channel blocker than lidocaine
Bupivacaine is less protein-bound than lidocaine

subject: ENT
stem: A 19-year-old man has severe sore throat, trismus, muffled hot-potato voice and deviation of the uvula to the right. What is the most appropriate management?
opts: Incision and drainage of the peritonsillar abscess

subject: ENT
topic: Digoxin toxicity — hypokalemia as the precipitating factor
stem: A 67-year-old woman on digoxin and furosemide for heart failure presents with nausea, anorexia, and yellow-green visual halos. She has had loose stools for 3 days after a course of antibiotics. The ECG shows sinus rhythm with characteristic ‘scooped’ ST segments. Which electrolyte abnormality most likely precipitated her toxicity?

subject: ENT
topic: MRI of the internal auditory meatus with gadolinium contrast
stem: A 48-year-old man has 4 months of slowly progressive hearing loss and constant tinnitus in his RIGHT ear only, with occasional dizziness. Audiometry shows right sensorineural loss. What is the most appropriate investigation?
opts: MRI of the internal auditory meatus with gadolinium contrast

subject: ENT
topic: Diabetic macular edema - anti-VEGF injections (ranibizumab, bevacizumab, aflibercept)
stem: A 55-year-old diabetic woman presents with blurring of central vision. Dilated examination shows hard exudates involving the macula in both eyes. What is the diagnosis, and which treatment is now FIRST-LINE?
opts: Cystoid macular edema from cataract - vitrectomy
Diabetic macular edema - anti-VEGF injections (ranibizumab, bevacizumab, aflibercept)

subject: ENT
stem: A 45-year-old man has severe episodes of dizziness with vomiting and right-sided ear pain, occurring in bursts lasting minutes to hours, with fluctuating hearing loss and tinnitus. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

stem: A 7-year-old boy presents with a 2-week history of repetitive sneezing, clear nasal discharge, and itchy eyes during the spring season. Physical examination reveals pale, boggy nasal mucosa. Which immunoglobulin is primarily involved in mediating this patient's condition?

subject: ENT
stem: A 16-month-old child suddenly develops noisy breathing and a cough while playing on the floor. He is afebrile. On examination there is unilateral wheeze with reduced air entry on one side. What is the most likely diagnosis?

subject: ENT
topic: Malignant (necrotizing) otitis externa — diabetic + granulation + CN VII palsy
stem: A 68-year-old male with poorly controlled diabetes presents with severe right ear pain for 3 weeks and scanty purulent discharge. Otoscopy shows granulation tissue at the bony-cartilaginous junction of the ear canal. He now has right-sided facial weakness. What is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Topical antibiotic ear drops and review in 1 week
CT scan of the temporal bone and IV antipseudomonal antibiotics

subject: ENT

opts: Anterior nasal packing with a different material

subject: ENT
topic: Posterior packing with a Foley balloon catheter plus ENT consultation
stem: A 72-year-old man with an active right-sided nosebleed has blood trickling down the posterior pharynx and no visible bleeding point on anterior rhinoscopy despite adequate pressure. What is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Posterior packing with a Foley balloon catheter plus ENT consultation
Discharge with petroleum jelly and follow-up
Bilateral silver nitrate cautery of the septum
Anterior packing with Merocel ribbon gauze

subject: ENT
topic: Ear, nose and throat disorders and ENT emergencies

stem: A 7-year-old child presents with epistaxis. Which of the following is the correct first-aid position?
opts: Tilt the head back and pinch the nostrils
Lie the child flat on their back

Place ice pack on the back of the neck

subject: ENT
stem: A 4-year-old girl is brought to the clinic due to a painful right ear, irritability, and a cough. She has a temperature of 38.8°C and right ear discharge. Otoscopy reveals an erythematous tympanic membrane with absence of the light reflex. What is the SINGLE most likely diagnosis?

stem: A 45-year-old male with diabetic ketoacidosis presents with facial pain, nasal obstruction, and a black necrotic eschar on the nasal mucosa. He is febrile and confused. What is the most urgent management step?
opts: Urgent surgical debridement and IV amphotericin B

subject: ENT

opts: Systemic ceftriaxone 1 g IM/IV plus saline irrigation

stem: A 70-year-old woman presents with a rapidly enlarging neck mass over 6 weeks, causing hoarseness, dysphagia, and stridor. The mass is hard, fixed to surrounding tissues, and there are multiple hard cervical lymph nodes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

MRI of the internal auditory meatus

opts: Nasal foreign body; careful anterior rhinoscopy and removal under proper visualization

opts: MRI of the internal auditory meatus with gadolinium

subject: ENT
topic: Sudden sensorineural hearing loss - urgent oral corticosteroid

Lateral neck X-ray to look for the thumb sign
Emergent controlled intubation in the operating room by anesthesia and ENT
IV antibiotics before any airway intervention

subject: ENT

Urgent audiometry, and if sudden sensorineural hearing loss is confirmed, high-dose oral prednisolone (60 mg daily) started within 72 hours

Drooling with tripod positioning and a muffled voice WITHOUT cough

stem: A 55-year-old diabetic man has a non-clearing vitreous hemorrhage of 4 weeks' duration with a confirmed attached retina on B-scan. What is the most appropriate initial management?
opts: Observation with head elevation at 30-45 degrees, avoid Valsalva, and strict diabetic control; panretinal photocoagulation later

opts: Herpes simplex type 1 (gingivostomatitis/ eczema herpetic…, oropharyngitis)

subject: EYE

opts: Relative afferent pupillary defect on the left

subject: EYE

No treatment — most childhood esotropia resolves spontaneously

subject: EYE

subject: EYE

subject: EYE
